chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Sulayman ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

For the nutfah (drop of fluid), twenty dinars; and for the alaqah (clot), forty dinars; and for the mudghah (chewed lump), sixty dinars; and for the 'azm (bones), eighty dinars. When the flesh covers it, one hundred dinars; then it remains one hundred until it bleeds (takes breath). When it bleeds, the diya (blood money) is complete.

key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or compensation for death/injury
key_terms.عَظْم: Stage of fetal development involving bones
key_terms.مُضْغَة: Third stage of fetal development (chewed lump)
key_terms.نَطْفَة: First stage of fetal development (drop of fluid)
key_terms.يَسْتَهِلّ: To bleed or take the first breath

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for a fetus at different stages of development in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s chain details the graduated blood money (diya) for a fetus, reflecting the Shia juristic view that compensation scales with developmental stages from nutfah to 'alqa. The transition to full diya upon 'istihlal (bleeding or first breath) underscores the biological markers used in Shia fiqh to determine fetal viability and inheritance rights.
